surprises.description: Amkor reported Q3 revenue of about $1.99 billion, below the preview’s $2.02–2.04 billion consensus range. Sequential growth was 5%, versus roughly 7% implied by the preview’s consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue reached approximately $1.99 billion, up 5% sequentially.”

surprises.description: Q3 gross margin was 18.3%, below both the 18.5% lower end of prior guidance and the preview’s roughly 19% consensus. The 150-basis-point sequential expansion was also less than the preview’s implied roughly 220 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded to 18.3%, up 150 basis points sequentially and 400 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists Q3 guidance of “18.5% – 19.5%” and consensus of “~19.0%”; it also gives implied year-over-year expansion of “+~470bps” from Q3'25 actual gross margin of 14.3%.

surprises.description: Q3 EPS of $0.76 missed the preview’s $0.78–0.79 consensus and was further below the $0.82 whisper number. Net income, by contrast, landed within the preview’s estimated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net income was $191 million with EPS of $0.76.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gives diluted EPS consensus of “$0.78” or “$0.79” and a “$0.82” whisper number; estimated net income is “$180M – $205M.”

surprises.description: Q3 computing grew 25% sequentially, short of the roughly 30% growth investors were led to expect. Amkor attributed the shortfall to the extended time needed to load its HDFO production line.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Computing revenue grew 25% sequentially to a new record, though this fell short of the ~30% growth guided last quarter due to the extended time needed to load the 300+ step HDFO production line.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s segment table gives Q3 computing growth of “+~30%”; it also says to watch for computing revenue of “≈$540M (+~30% q/q).”

surprises.description: Amkor’s Q4 revenue outlook has a $1.95 billion midpoint, below the preview’s $2.04 billion consensus, and its $1.9–2.0 billion range includes outcomes materially below that consensus. This is a weaker outlook than the preview’s expected essentially flat sequential revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 revenue is guided to $1.9-2.0 billion,” implying “a flat-to-slightly-down sequential outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4'26 consensus is $0.78 EPS / $2.04B revenue — essentially flat sequentially”; the preview’s base case also anticipated Q4 revenue of “$1.95–2.05B (≈in line).”

surprises.description: Q4 gross-margin guidance of 18–19% is weaker than the preview’s roughly 19–20% benchmark, with the guide midpoint below 19%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 revenue is guided to $1.9-2.0 billion with gross margin of 18-19%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview ranks “Q4'26 revenue + GM guidance vs. $2.04B / ~19–20%” as the key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Q4 EPS guidance of $0.65–0.75 is below the preview’s $0.78 consensus, including at the top of the company’s range.

Amkor now expects consumer revenue to fall more than seasonally in Q4, into the mid-teens percentage range sequentially, due to shortages affecting premium-tier smartphones. The preview discussed Q3 consumer growth but did not flag this Q4 decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumer revenue is expected to decline more than seasonally into the mid-teens percent sequentially in Q4 due to component shortages affecting premium-tier smartphones.”

surprises.description: Management gave a notably strong longer-term computing outlook: full-year 2026 growth is expected to exceed 30%, with a similar or higher rate into 2027. The preview focused on the Q3 ramp and execution risk but did not state this sustained growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Computing is expected to grow low double digits sequentially in Q4, resulting in over 50% year-over-year growth, with full-year 2026 computing growth exceeding 30% and expected to continue at a similar or higher rate into 2027.”

surprises.description: Amkor said customer prepayments and its balance sheet can fund investment without incremental debt through 2027, a reassuring financing detail not established in the preview. The preview already anticipated roughly $3 billion of prepayments, so the surprise is the stated debt-free funding capacity rather than the prepayment total.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer advance payment arrangements have been executed with a dozen customers since 2025 … bringing prepayments to roughly $3 billion,” and “the balance sheet [is] positioned to fund investment without incremental debt through 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “$3B total” in NVIDIA prepayments and flagged “how/when the NVIDIA prepayments land in cash flow”; it also noted “$2.5B cash vs. $2.5B debt.”

surprises.description: The 2026 capital-spending outlook was narrowed to around $2.5 billion, the low end of the preview’s expected $2.5–3.0 billion range. That is a somewhat lighter 2026 spending outlook than the upper end investors were watching for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2026 CapEx was narrowed to around $2.5 billion.”

surprises.description: Management outlined a substantial 2027 facilities-spending step-up, with more than $2 billion in facility spending alone and Arizona spending expected to peak in 2028–2029. The preview discussed major investment plans and Arizona underutilization risk, but did not give this facilities-spending scale or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A significant step-up [is] expected in 2027 (over $2 billion from facilities alone: up to 15% of Arizona's $12 billion plan, $400-450 million in Korea, $50 million in Vietnam), and Arizona spend is expected to peak in 2028-2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Capex and free cash flow” and “Arizona as a margin headwind in 2027 and 2028 from underutilization,” but did not quantify 2027 facilities spending.
